the integrins alpha 1 to alpha6 are differentially expressed in stromal cells and that extracellular matrix components are predominantly found within the stroma of lymphoid tissues.

the beta 1-integrins are not expressed on the majority of the cells of the immune system but that their expression is restricted to stromal cells and that their extracellular ligand(s) are predominantly associated with the extracellular matrix of the lymphoid stroma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression pattern of beta 1-integrins in human lymphoid tissue can be divided into four categories.
beta 1 integrin expression by stromal cells is highly regulated, both in terms of the type of beta 1 chain expressed and the type of extracellular matrix protein bound.
beta 1 integrin and their ligands are expressed in a cell type and tissue specific manner and that they are involved in the maintenance of tissue structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of beta 1-integrins and extracellular matrix ligand is not uniform in lymphoid tissues.

the expression of beta 1-integrin subunits and extracellular ligands is differentially regulated in human lymphoid tissue, suggesting that the expression of these proteins is not merely a reflection of the tissue type, but is also regulated by the local microenvironment.
the expression of integrins and extracellular matrix ligand is highly restricted to the stromal cells of the lymphoid organs.
